question: My FASTag balance has gone below zero even though I had money in it before crossing the toll. How did this happen and how do I fix it?

evidence_groups.quote: Deferred toll deductions — some toll plazas process transactions 24-48 hours after the vehicle passage
Top up the FASTag wallet to clear the negative balance and restore functionality

reference_answer: A FASTag can go negative when toll deductions are processed 24-48 hours late, when a plaza charges a double-toll penalty because the tag was unreadable, or because of a minimum balance some issuers apply. Top up the wallet to clear the negative balance, check the transaction history to find the deduction, and dispute it on ihmcl.com or 1033 if it is wrong. Enabling auto-recharge prevents it happening again.
key_facts: deferred toll deductions processed 24-48 hours later
penalty (double toll) when the tag was unreadable
top up the wallet to clear the negative balance
check transaction history; dispute wrong charges via ihmcl.com or 1033
enable auto-recharge to prevent it

question: The toll plaza deducted my FASTag twice for one crossing. How do I raise a dispute to get the duplicate amount back?

evidence_groups.quote: Log a dispute with your FASTag issuer bank (the bank that issued your FASTag)
If the bank doesn't resolve in 7 working days, escalate to RBI CMS

reference_answer: Keep the toll receipt as evidence, then log a dispute with the bank that issued your FASTag with the date, plaza name and both amounts. You can also raise it on ihmcl.com (Help & Support, Raise a Dispute) or call the NHAI helpline 1033. If the bank doesn't resolve it in 7 working days, escalate to RBI CMS; most duplicates are reversed within 5-7 working days.
key_facts: keep the toll receipt as evidence
dispute with the FASTag issuer bank
ihmcl.com or helpline 1033
escalate to RBI CMS if unresolved in 7 working days

question: How much can I keep in UPI Lite, what is the per-payment limit, and do these payments use up my daily UPI limit?

evidence_groups.quote: up to ₹2,000 balance) for making quick payments up to ₹500 per transaction
It allows you to make payments up to ₹500 without requiring UPI PIN for each transaction
UPI Lite transactions are not part of the UPI daily limit count

reference_answer: UPI Lite holds up to ₹2,000 and each payment can be up to ₹500 without a UPI PIN; larger amounts go through regular UPI with a PIN. UPI Lite payments don't count towards the daily UPI limit.
key_facts: balance up to ₹2,000
up to ₹500 per payment
no UPI PIN for these payments
not counted in the daily UPI limit
notes: Needs two facts; the daily-limit fact is only in kb_0687.

question: Fraudsters swapped my SIM and took ₹80,000 through UPI. The bank says I'm responsible. Is that right, and what should I do?

evidence_groups.quote: and you report it within three working days, your liability is limited or nil depending on the transaction amount
Immediately file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in and call 1930

reference_answer: Not necessarily. Under RBI's limited-liability circular, a SIM swap without your negligence is usually a third-party breach; if you report it within three working days your liability is limited or nil. It changes if you shared an OTP. File at cybercrime.gov.in, call 1930, get a written record of the SIM swap from your operator, and complain to the bank in writing citing circular RBI/2017-18/15.
key_facts: SIM swap counts as a third-party breach
reported within three working days, liability is limited or nil
sharing an OTP changes the assessment
complain at cybercrime.gov.in and call 1930
written complaint to the bank citing RBI/2017-18/15

question: What is the transaction limit on UPI 123Pay, and how does *99# work without internet?

evidence_groups.quote: Dial *99# on any mobile phone connected to any network

reference_answer: UPI 123Pay works through voice prompts on an IVR call and the transaction limit is ₹10,000 per transaction. *99# is USSD: you dial *99# from your bank-registered number and a text menu lets you check balance, send money and see a mini statement without internet, in Hindi and 12 other regional languages.
key_facts: ₹10,000 per transaction
*99# is USSD and needs no internet
dial from the bank-registered mobile number
check balance, send money, mini statement

question: My father died in an accident and was covered under PMSBY. Which documents do we need for the claim and is there a deadline?

evidence_groups.quote: The claim-cum-discharge form must be submitted to the bank branch within 30 days of the accident
Death certificate, FIR copy (for accidental death), post-mortem report

reference_answer: Submit the claim-cum-discharge form at the branch where PMSBY was enrolled within 30 days of the accident, with the death certificate, FIR, post-mortem report, hospital summary if any, and the nominee's Aadhaar and bank details. The ₹2 lakh goes to the registered nominee; without a nomination it goes to legal heirs, who may need a succession certificate. Delays beyond 30 days can be escalated to the Insurance Ombudsman.
key_facts: claim form at the bank branch within 30 days of the accident
death certificate, FIR and post-mortem report
nominee's Aadhaar and bank details
₹2 lakh to the nominee, or legal heirs if none

question: Does it cost anything to complain to the RBI Ombudsman, and when am I allowed to file?

evidence_groups.quote: There is absolutely NO fee to file a complaint
The bank has not responded within 30 days of your complaint

reference_answer: It is free. You can file if the bank hasn't responded within 30 days of your complaint or you're unhappy with its reply, online at cms.rbi.org.in or by calling 14440. The Ombudsman can award up to ₹30 lakh for financial loss plus ₹1 lakh for harassment.
key_facts: no fee
bank has not replied within 30 days, or reply unsatisfactory
cms.rbi.org.in or 14440
up to ₹30 lakh plus ₹1 lakh compensation

question: My EMI auto-debit bounced because of a glitch at the bank, even though I had enough money, and they charged me a bounce fee. Can I get it reversed?

evidence_groups.quote: charges can only be levied for NACH failures caused by the customer
Get the bank's admission of technical error in writing

reference_answer: Yes. Charges can only be levied when the customer caused the NACH failure, so a bank-side technical error is a deficiency of service and both the bounce charge and any late-payment penalty must be reversed. Get the bank's admission in writing, complain with your balance on that date, and go to RBI CMS if it isn't reversed within 7 days; tell the lender so nothing is reported to the credit bureau.
key_facts: charges only for customer-caused failures
bounce charge and late penalty must be reversed
get the bank's admission of technical error in writing
RBI CMS if not reversed within 7 days
notes: Does not name NACH; tests paraphrase matching.

question: My bank says a failed UPI payment takes 7-10 business days to refund. What are the official timelines?

evidence_groups.quote: must happen within T+1 business day automatically
Bank-level dispute resolution (when you raise a complaint) must be resolved within 3 business days

reference_answer: Failed UPI payments must be auto-reversed within T+1 business day. A dispute you raise with the bank must be resolved within 3 business days, and an NPCI-level escalation within 5. The 7-10 days quoted is not compliant; if exceeded you can complain at cms.rbi.org.in.
key_facts: auto-reversal within T+1 business day
bank dispute resolved within 3 business days
NPCI escalation within 5 business days
7-10 days is non-compliant; Ombudsman via cms.rbi.org.in
